answer_1.quote: We introduce a new Reference Image to Slide Generation task and a novel Slide Complexity Metric for evaluating slide complexity. Based on this metric, we build the Slide2Code benchmark with different levels of difficulty. We also propose SlideCoder enhanced by a Color Gradient-based Segmentation algorithm, a Layout-aware Prompt and a Hierarchical Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation for accurate slide generation.
answer_1.outputs: Python code for generating slides using python-pptx library

answer_2.quote: To comprehensively assess generation quality, we adopt four metrics, using the notations defined in §3.1. (1) Global Visual Metrics, including CLIP and SSIM scores computed between the original image I 0 and the generated image I g ; (2) Local Structural Metrics, which compare the original and generated slide files F 0 and F g in terms of content similarity and position similarity, following ; (3) Execution, defined as the success rate of executing C g without errors; and (4) Overall Score, calculated as the average of all metric values across all samples, with failed executions assigned a score of zero.

answer_4.quote: To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed Slide Complexity Metric (SCM), we conducted a human subject study. A total of 100 samples were randomly selected from the Slide2Code benchmark for evaluation. Four doctoral students were recruited as annotators, each assigned 50 slides to assess.
answer_4.guideline: The annotators were instructed to score each slide from the perspective of three dimensions: the number of shapes, the diversity of shape types, and the level of element coverage. The scoring range was 0-100, following the protocol in Appendix D.
